meta.title: Benchmarks — fly brains vs trading bots
meta.description: Real fruit-fly brains against trading bots, an LLM bot and buy-and-hold, on the same 30 days of Robinhood Chain prices at the same costs. Every result, the method and the caveats.

head.title: Fly brains vs trading bots
head.lede: We put real fruit-fly brains against trading bots on the same tokens, the same real Robinhood Chain prices and the same costs. Every result is on this page, including the flies that lost.

r1.lede: Our first run, two weeks at the end of the month above, same rules. The market fell 10.2%; the best fly beat it by 5.9 points and three of the six flies beat it.

flies.lede: Six flies, each its own brain with its own settings, traded the same 30 days. Two beat the market, and every one of the six lost less than every trading bot.

shows.good_h: Every fly lost less than every bot
shows.good_p: The best bot lost 53% over the month; the worst fly lost 34% and the best only 15%. The bots lost mostly to churn: rotating the wallet every 12 hours costs 0.3–1% a swap on these thin pools, and each bot paid $300–900 in costs. The flies trade smaller, pay about 0.12% a fill, and sat out more of a falling market.
shows.bad_h: Not every fly beat the market
shows.bad_p: Two of the six flies beat the market over the month, and three of six in the two-week round. Each fly trades with its own settings, and a longer window shows which settings hold up. Every fly is listed on this page.
shows.llm_p: A language model shown each token's recent moves and asked what to hold, every 12 hours, lost 78% over the month. It came last in both rounds: no edge, and the churn costs the rest.

rules.p1: Prices: 15-minute candles of every token on fly.ai's list, from GeckoTerminal, used every 45 minutes (the live flies' pace).
rules.p2: Costs, on every trade, for everyone: the pool fee, price impact from each pool's real depth (constant product), and $0.05 gas.
rules.p3: Flies: the live fly brain (the full connectome, all learning on), six flies with their own settings.
rules.p4: Bots: buy-and-hold (every token, equal weight, bought once); momentum and reversal (every 12 h, hold the 3 tokens that rose or fell most over 24 h); random (3 random tokens every 12 h, averaged over 20 runs); the LLM bot (every 12 h, a language model picks up to 3 tokens from their 2 h, 6 h and 24 h moves). Bots only trade pools deep enough for their size.
rules.caveat: Two windows so far, both in a falling market. A ranking here is what happened on these prices, not proof of an edge. We will keep running it on new windows and publish the result either way.

chart.how: each bar is a return minus the market's

m1.lede: Everyone started with the same paper wallet and paid the same pool fee, price impact and gas on every trade. The market (every token held from its first price) fell 17.9%.
